name: social-media-backend

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers can generate massive amounts of traffic targeting the public endpoints, potentially exhausting resources and preventing legitimate users from accessing the service.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: A botnet could be used to generate thousands of requests per second to the ALB or API Gateway endpoints, overwhelming the system's capacity to handle legitimate traffic.

recommendations.description: Implement AWS Shield Advanced for DDoS protection
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable AWS Shield Advanced for the CloudFront distribution, ALB, and API Gateway. Configure AWS Shield Advanced with automatic application layer DDoS mitigation.

recommendations.description: Implement rate limiting at multiple layers
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure WAF rate-based rules, API Gateway throttling, and CloudFront viewer request policies to limit request rates per IP/user.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: AWS Shield Advanced integrates with AWS WAF and provides additional protection against SYN floods, UDP floods, and other reflection attacks. It also includes DDoS cost protection and 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT).

ground_truth.threatName: Single Point of Failure in Load Balancer Configuration

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: If the ALB experiences issues or becomes overwhelmed, all incoming traffic would be affected as there's no redundancy in the load balancing layer.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: A targeted attack or technical failure affecting the ALB could disrupt all incoming traffic to the application, even if the backend services remain healthy.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Deploy multiple ALBs across different Availability Zones with Route 53 DNS failover routing policy. Update the CDK stack to create redundant ALBs.
Deploy the application stack in multiple regions with Route 53 geolocation or latency-based routing.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using AWS Global Accelerator for improved availability and performance across regions. Route 53 health checks can be used to automatically failover between ALBs or regions.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Without a service mesh, services communicate directly over the network without enforced encryption or strong mutual authentication, potentially allowing unauthorized access or eavesdropping.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who gains access to the VPC could potentially intercept inter-service communication or impersonate a service to gain unauthorized access to other services.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Deploy AWS App Mesh to enforce TLS encryption and mutual authentication between services. Configure Envoy proxies as sidecars in ECS tasks.
Use AWS IAM roles for service-to-service authentication and implement JWT-based service authentication.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: AWS App Mesh integrates with AWS Certificate Manager for TLS certificate management and AWS X-Ray for end-to-end request tracing and visualization.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Each service instance creates its own database connections without pooling, potentially exhausting database connection limits during high load or attack scenarios.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could trigger multiple rapid requests causing services to create many database connections, exhausting the connection pool and causing service disruption.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use PgBouncer or Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora PostgreSQL connections. Configure appropriate pool sizes and timeout settings.
Set up CloudWatch alarms for database connection counts and configure automatic scaling based on connection metrics.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Amazon RDS Proxy provides built-in connection pooling and can help reduce failover times for Aurora databases. It also supports IAM authentication and encryption in transit.

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Services accessing AWS APIs through public endpoints expose traffic to potential interception and make the system vulnerable to credential theft and unauthorized access.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who compromises a service could potentially access AWS services through public endpoints, even if they gain access to valid credentials, as there's no network-level restriction.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Deploy interface and gateway endpoints for all AWS services used by the application. Update security groups and routing tables accordingly.
Configure VPC endpoint policies to restrict access to specific resources and actions. Use resource-based policies where applicable.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS PrivateLink for services that don't support gateway endpoints. Consider costs associated with interface endpoints versus data transfer through public endpoints.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Sensitive credentials and configuration values might be exposed through environment variables or configuration files rather than being properly managed through Secrets Manager.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who gains access to the ECS task definitions or environment variables could potentially extract sensitive credentials.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Move all sensitive values to AWS Secrets Manager, including database credentials, API keys, and service-to-service authentication tokens.
Configure automatic rotation for supported secret types and implement custom rotation for others.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Secrets Manager's built-in integration with Aurora for database credential rotation. Consider using AWS Parameter Store for non-sensitive configuration values to optimize costs.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
AWS Architecture Diagram for Social Media Platform Backend
This diagram illustrates a microservices-based architecture for a social media platform,
including CDN, load balancing, containerization, authentication, databases, and monitoring.
"""

# Network & Content Delivery
from diagrams.aws.network import CloudFront, ALB, APIGateway
from diagrams.aws.network import VPC, InternetGateway, NATGateway

# Compute & Containers
from diagrams.aws.compute import ECS, EKS
from diagrams.aws.compute import Fargate

# Security & Identity
from diagrams.aws.security import Cognito
from diagrams.aws.security import WAF

# Database & Storage
from diagrams.aws.database import Aurora
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb
from diagrams.aws.database import ElastiCache
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3

# Analytics & Search
from diagrams.aws.analytics import Analytics
from diagrams.aws.analytics import ES

# Management & Monitoring
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch
from diagrams.aws.management import AutoScaling

# Core imports
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.aws.general import Client

# Custom styling
DIAGRAM_ATTRS = {
    "fontsize": "30",
    "bgcolor": "white",
    "splines": "ortho",  # Use orthogonal lines for clearer labels
    "nodesep": "1.5",    # Increase horizontal spacing
    "ranksep": "2.0",    # Increase vertical spacing
    "pad": "3.0",
    "concentrate": "true",  # Reduce edge crossings
    "labelspacing": "1.0",  # Control spacing between labels
    "labeljust": "l",      # Left-justify labels
    "labelloc": "t"        # Place labels at top
}

NODE_ATTRS = {
    "fontsize": "13",
    "margin": "0.6",
    "width": "1",
    "height": "1",
}

EDGE_ATTRS = {
    "fontsize": "11",
    "minlen": "2",
    "penwidth": "1.5",
    "labelangle": "25",    # Control label angle
    "labeldistance": "2.0" # Control label distance from edge
}

# Edge labels for different flows
EDGE_LABELS = {
    "request": "HTTP/HTTPS Request",
    "cdn": "Static Content Delivery",
    "auth": "OAuth2/OIDC Flow\nJWT Token Generation",
    "api": "REST API Calls",
    "data_write": "Primary Data Write\nSync Operations",
    "data_read": "Read Operations",
    "cache": "In-Memory Cache",
    "media": "Media Upload/Download\nS3 Presigned URLs",
    "event": "Async Event Stream",
    "monitor": "Metrics & Traces",
    "scale": "Auto-scaling Events"
}

EDGE_STYLES = {
    "request": {"color": "blue", "style": "solid", "label": EDGE_LABELS["request"]},
    "cdn": {"color": "blue", "style": "solid", "label": EDGE_LABELS["cdn"]},
    "auth": {"color": "green", "style": "dashed", "label": EDGE_LABELS["auth"]},
    "api": {"color": "black", "style": "solid", "label": EDGE_LABELS["api"]},
    "data": {"color": "red", "style": "solid", "label": EDGE_LABELS["data_write"]},
    "read": {"color": "red", "style": "dashed", "label": EDGE_LABELS["data_read"]},
    "cache": {"color": "orange", "style": "dashed", "label": EDGE_LABELS["cache"]},
    "media": {"color": "purple", "style": "bold", "label": EDGE_LABELS["media"]},
    "event": {"color": "purple", "style": "dashed", "label": EDGE_LABELS["event"]},
    "monitor": {"color": "gray", "style": "dashed", "label": EDGE_LABELS["monitor"]},
    "scale": {"color": "gray", "style": "dotted", "label": EDGE_LABELS["scale"]}
}

def create_social_media_architecture():
    """Creates the AWS architecture diagram for the social media platform."""
    
    with Diagram(
        "Social Media Platform Architecture",
        filename="social_media_architecture",
        direction="TB",
        outformat="png",
        graph_attr=DIAGRAM_ATTRS,
        node_attr=NODE_ATTRS,
        edge_attr=EDGE_ATTRS,
        show=False
    ):
        # Define clients/users
        users = Client("End Users")

        # AWS Account boundary
        with Cluster("AWS Account"):
            # Public Security Zone
            with Cluster("Public Security Zone"):
                # Content Delivery and API Layer
                with Cluster("Content Delivery & API Layer"):
                    cdn = CloudFront("CloudFront CDN")
                    waf = WAF("WAF")
                    alb = ALB("Application\nLoad Balancer")
                    api = APIGateway("API Gateway")

                # Authentication & Security
                with Cluster("Authentication"):
                    cognito = Cognito("Amazon Cognito")

            # Private Security Zone
            with Cluster("Private Security Zone"):
                # Container Orchestration
                with Cluster("Container Orchestration"):
                    with Cluster("ECS/EKS Cluster"):
                        user_svc = ECS("User Service")
                        content_svc = ECS("Content Service")
                        social_svc = ECS("Social Service")
                        notif_svc = ECS("Notification Service")
                        fargate = Fargate("Fargate")

                # Monitoring & Scaling
                with Cluster("Operations"):
                    monitoring = Cloudwatch("CloudWatch")
                    autoscaling = AutoScaling("Auto Scaling")

                # Data Storage Layer
                with Cluster("Data Storage"):
                    # Primary Storage
                    with Cluster("Primary Storage"):
                        aurora = Aurora("Aurora\n(User Data)")
                        dynamo = Dynamodb("DynamoDB\n(Sessions)")
                    
                    # Caching & Media
                    with Cluster("Caching & Media"):
                        redis = ElastiCache("ElastiCache\n(Redis)")
                        s3 = S3("S3\n(Media)")

                    # Analytics & Search
                    with Cluster("Analytics & Events"):
                        elasticsearch = ES("Elasticsearch\n(Search)")
                        kafka = Analytics("MSK\n(Kafka)")

            # Define connections with labels
            users >> Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["request"],
                tailport="s",
                headport="n"
            ) >> cdn

            # Add consistent edge routing for main flow
            for idx, (src, dst) in enumerate([
                (cdn, waf),
                (waf, alb),
                (alb, api)
            ]):
                src >> Edge(
                    xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["cdn"],
                    tailport="s",
                    headport="n"
                ) >> dst

            # Group similar services with aligned edges
            for service in [user_svc, content_svc, social_svc, notif_svc]:
                api >> Edge(
                    xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["api"],
                    tailport="s",
                    headport="n"
                ) >> service

            # Align database connections
            with Cluster("Data Connections"):
                user_svc >> Edge(
                    xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["data_write"],
                    tailport="e",
                    headport="w"
                ) >> aurora

                content_svc >> Edge(
                    xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["data_write"],
                    tailport="e",
                    headport="w"
                ) >> dynamo

            # Authentication flow
            api >> Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["auth"],
                tailport="e",
                headport="w"
            ) >> cognito

            # Analytics and search connections
            content_svc >> Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["event"],
                tailport="e",
                headport="w"
            ) >> elasticsearch

            social_svc >> Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["event"],
                tailport="e",
                headport="w"
            ) >> kafka

            # Cache and media connections
            social_svc >> Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["cache"],
                tailport="e",
                headport="w"
            ) >> redis

            notif_svc >> Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["media"],
                tailport="e",
                headport="w"
            ) >> s3

            # Monitoring and scaling connections
            monitoring << Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["monitor"],
                tailport="w",
                headport="e"
            ) << user_svc

            autoscaling >> Edge(
                xlabel=EDGE_LABELS["scale"],
                tailport="e",
                headport="w"
            ) >> content_svc

            # Align Fargate connections
            for service in [user_svc, content_svc, social_svc, notif_svc]:
                fargate >> Edge(
                    style="dotted",
                    color="black",
                    label="Container Deployment",
                    xlabel="Container Deployment",
                    tailport="e",
                    headport="w"
                ) >> service

if __name__ == "__main__":
    create_social_media_architecture()
